trust_decision.summary: Whether the client-supplied site URL (the ?ref= on session context, which is carried through the SSO state/RelayState and parsed back on the callback) is a trusted origin before the server issues a 303 redirect carrying freshly minted access/refresh tokens to that origin. It is decided nowhere at the pinned commit; the fix adds global.Config.IsOriginAllowed and calls it in implsession at the ref and callback steps.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'OAuth state manipulation, session token theft'. The token-bearing redirect URL is built here from callbackIdentity.State.URL, so this is the first place an engineer would look.

fix_sites.module_kind: core session module (login-URL / state producer step)

fix_sites.entry_point: config loading (global::allowed_origins, YAML or env) plus the new public method Config.IsOriginAllowed
fix_sites.module_kind: global config package (looks out of scope)

fix_sites.entry_point: constructor NewModule gains a global.Config parameter

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/global/config.go:17-53 (Config struct, newConfig defaults, Validate); the fix adds an allow-list key with an allow-all default when unset (fix.diff:98-101) and validates its entries (fix.diff:85-93)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The SAML/OIDC/Google provider packages already build the state and seem to own it, so a solver could patch only the callback redirect at module.go:179 and treat the ref check at session-context time (which only returns an IdP login URL and never redirects) plus the global config allow-list as unnecessary.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: IdP-initiated SAML uses a host-less relative RelayState ('login'). The callback check is skipped when State.URL.Host is empty (fix.diff:305), and when allowed_origins is unset all origins stay allowed (fix.diff:99-101). A blanket 'state must carry an allow-listed host' rule, or a default-deny, would break IdP-initiated SAML login and existing installs that have no allowed_origins.

O6_input_shapes: absolute URL with a foreign host
host-less relative state (skipped by design at the callback)

O7_producer.where: pkg/config/conf.go:67-72 (StringToSliceHookFunc(',') and StringToURLHookFunc at pkg/config/conf.go:107-124 decode global::allowed_origins into []*url.URL); state producer authtypes.NewState pkg/types/authtypes/authn.go:57-71

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the error redirect gains a 'next'/return-to parameter taken from the callback query or state and is redirected to without the origin check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Returning users to where they came from after a failed SSO is a common UX request, and the helper already builds redirect URLs from request-derived data.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second state parser (e.g. a base64/JSON-encoded state for a new provider) whose URL bypasses the Host!='' gate, a separator or identity differential on the protected item
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Providers each parse their own state field (state vs RelayState); a new provider with its own encoding is a plausible addition.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: IdP-initiated SAML RelayState built with an absolute URL taken from the auth domain's stored config (save/reload of a domain field) rather than the relative 'login'
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Admins host the UI on a different origin than the API; a stored 'redirect after IdP login' field on the auth domain is a natural feature, and it crosses a DB save/reload boundary the check never calls.

O9_family: open redirect / token leakage via unvalidated OAuth/SAML state (CWE-601, CWE-345)

O10_build.project_tests: pkg/global/config_test.go (TestValidate only at the pinned commit); there are no unit tests for pkg/modules/session/implsession or the callback authn packages at the pinned commit. Module-level tests need fakes for authNs, the authdomain store, the tokenizer and the user setter.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Compare the callback State.URL host against the request Host or external_url at module.go:179, or force a relative redirect. This leaves the ref step open, breaks deployments where the UI and API are on different origins, and invents no configurable allow-list.

out_of_scope_notes: Fix commit 8c6a0de8 only edits a GCP Memorystore dashboard JSON (fix.diff:1-35) and is unrelated to the advisory.

Google/OIDC oauth2 redirect_uri and the SAML ACS URL are derived from the unvalidated state host (pkg/authn/callbackauthn/googlecallbackauthn/authn.go:182-186, ee/authn/callbackauthn/samlcallbackauthn/authn.go:139). This is a token-exchange parameter, not the redirect sink; not pursued.
unverified: Possible how-type residual in the published fix, not verified because I could not read the Go stdlib source in this sandbox or run code. url.Parse('https:/evil.example/x') yields Host=='' (Go sets OmitHost). The callback gate is skipped when Host=='' (fix.diff:305), but module.go:179-184 rebuilds a fresh url.URL without OmitHost, so String() may emit 'https:///evil.example/x', which browsers resolve to evil.example. If this holds, it is a parser differential on the protected item's identity at the fix's own guard. Hidden tests could target it only if our copy fixes it too.
repo_mb not measured (no shell); signoz includes a large frontend tree, so the size is likely well above 5 MB, but tiny_repo/giant_repo were not assessed.

Fairness concern: the published fix introduces a new opt-in config key (global::allowed_origins) and a method name (IsOriginAllowed). Hidden tests that depend on that exact API would need the report to name it; with the key unset, behaviour is unchanged (allow-all).
